title: IoFailure wire form: decide between Debug-of-ErrorKind (current), hand-maintained u8 table, or drop kind entirely
description:
Follow-up to PKIX-tit4.4 (option (c) doc-correction shipped). The remaining question is whether the workspace's IoFailure { kind, message } shape (PKIX-2l0v.1 D3) is the right wire form long-term, or whether one of two stronger options should be taken pre-1.0:

(a) Replace format!("{:?}", kind) with a hand-maintained u8/string match table. New std::io::ErrorKind variants become a maintenance task on each stdlib bump; no silent lossy round-trip in practice (consumers without the entry emit/decode a sentinel that survives without losing fidelity).

(b) Drop the typed kind field entirely. IoFailure becomes { message: String }. Callers needing programmatic kind branching can grep the message or upgrade their oracle.

(c) [shipped via PKIX-tit4.4] Keep Debug-of-ErrorKind, but disclose the brittleness honestly in rustdoc. Currently in tree.

Workspace-level: PKIX-2l0v.1 D3 picked the { kind, message } shape; pkix-aia and pkix-truststore both follow it. Reversing to (b) is a workspace-wide breaking change. Decision wants human input because: pre-1.0 framing argues for design closure but D3 IS the design closure, and (a)/(b) reverse it. Recommendation if no human pushback within 24h: stay at (c). Cross-references PKIX-tit4.5 (which raises the question of whether IoFailure should be lifted to pkix-path); a (b) decision here would moot tit4.5 partially.
notes:
DECISION (2026-11-28, Mark): take option (a). Deferred, not done -- recorded here as work.

This bead's framing was wrong in a way that made the decision look harder than it is.

It presents (a) as reversing PKIX-2l0v.1 D3 and weighs pre-1.0 design closure against that. It does not reverse D3. D3 picked the { kind, message } shape; (a) keeps that shape exactly and changes only the serde function. There is no API change, no semver impact, and nothing for a consumer to notice.

And the table (a) would supposedly introduce already exists. pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs's io_error_kind_serde::deserialize is a hand-maintained match over 19 ErrorKind variants with '_ => Other'. Only serialize uses format!("{kind:?}").

That asymmetry is the real defect, and it is worse than the cross-version loss the rustdoc documents. The two halves do not agree by construction -- they agree because std's Debug happens to emit variant names. If that ever changed, serialize would emit a string this crate's own deserialize does not recognise, degrading to Other within a single version of this crate. The rustdoc describes skew between producer and consumer versions; it does not say the round-trip is self-consistent only by coincidence.

So (a) is: lift the 19 variants to one const table and drive both directions from it. Roughly 20 lines in one private module.

This is the third instance in one session of the same failure mode -- two halves of a relationship coupled only by a comment, after wildcard SAN vs dNSName constraints (PKIX-bhtl) and CN fallback vs the constraint check (PKIX-55jb). AGENTS.md now records the pattern under 'Two correct crates can compose into a vulnerability'; this is the cheap place to apply it.

(b) rejected: kind is useful in-process typing -- NotFound versus PermissionDenied on a trust store load is something a caller acts on -- and dropping it is a workspace-wide break for a problem that exists only in the opt-in serde path.
(c) superseded: honest documentation of a brittleness that can be removed for 20 lines is the worse trade once the table is known to exist.

Work remaining:
  - one const [(ErrorKind, &str); 19] table in io_error_kind_serde
  - serialize and deserialize both driven from it
  - a round-trip test over every entry, which is the test that makes the two halves agree by construction rather than by comment
  - rustdoc on IoFailure::kind updated: the remaining cost is only the version-skew one, not Debug instability
